message: In the twin under-deck Tuned Mass Damper (TMD, mass on spring with damper tuned to bridge mode) retrofit concept, the damper tuning has apparent conflict raised by Manager, thank you Manager. To check it I used vetted calculation with the Den Hartog optimum result (E3). I found 1.81 hertz with 64634 newtons per metre stiffness at 13.36 percent damper damping for 500 kilograms total mass, according to Den Hartog, 1934. I propose retaining 1.81 hertz for 5.0 percent mass ratio, thank you Structural Dynamics Lead. My position: ready because mass ratio reconciles tuning. In the same twin Tuned Mass Damper concept, the added damping ratio has verification need for comfort. To check it I used two-degree-of-freedom frequency response simulation with the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6). I found 9.44 percent effective damping rising from 0.4 percent inherent damping, according to Den Hartog, 1947. I propose retaining two 250 kilogram units on coil springs with viscous dampers hung below girders, thank you Retrofit Integration Architect. My position: ready because added damping is quantified. In the 40 metre footbridge retrofit concept, the vertical crowd acceleration has uncomfortable peaks. To check it I used the same response simulation with the two-degree-of-freedom response simulation (E6) and the under-deck twin-unit layout sketch (E7). I found reduction from 17.50 metres per second squared to 0.74 metres per second squared with 20.0 millimetres travel reaching Comfort Level (CL, Setra comfort grade) CL2, according to Setra, 2006.
